events.title: Mimi Chen Ting: Make Movement Visible
events.venue: Brigham Young University Museum of Art
events.description: April 10 to October 10, 2026This exhibition celebrates the life and work of Chinese American artist Mimi Chen Ting, whose dynamic paintings, prints, and performances from the 1960s to early 2020s continue to captivate audiences today. Over the span of five decades, Ting created a vibrant body of work that investigated movement in all forms: from the movement of the hand marking the surface of a canvas to the movement of bodies in space; from movements that organized musical compositions to the movement across oceans and borders that defined her lived experiences as an Asian American immigrant.

events.title: Museum Patio Program
events.venue: This program takes place behind the Zion Human History Museum on the shaded outdoor patio., Zion National Park
events.description: Sit back and relax while enjoying a short ranger talk on the shaded back patio of the Zion Human History Museum! In these programs, you will explore the resources that make Zion special. Topics may include geology, wildlife, plants, human history, and so much more. No two programs are quite the same! Accessibility information: This program takes place outdoors on a shaded patio. Wooden benches are available for seating, as well as space for mobility devices. Rangers at the visitor center are available for any questions. You can also visit our Accessibility page for more information.

events.description: Come join a Ranger at Sunset Point for a rim walk toward Sunrise Point. The talk will be on a random topic of the ranger's choosing, covering natural, cultural, or historical resources. Visitors meet Ranger at alcove to the right of Sunset Point overlook. This program will be cancelled by thunderstorms, extreme cold weather, or staffing shortages. Wheelchair Accessible.

Aaron Memmott captures the glow of cities at night, streetlights and wet pavement rendered in rich, atmospheric color. Patrick St. Clair turns to modernist interiors, where light becomes the bridge between the built world and the lives lived within it.
